production.note: US model years. First: the Porsche release reproduced by Conceptcarz (conceptcarz-2011-911-gt2-rs) calls it "the new 2011 Porsche 911 GT2 RS" and says it "will be available in the U.S. October 2010". KBB lists a "GT2 RS Coupe 2D" for 2011 (kbb-911-2011-specs) and a "2012 Porsche 911 GT2 RS Coupe 2D" (kbb-911-2012-specs; database), which is the end year used. Porsche's classic-model page (porsche-classic-997-gt2) dates the car "(2011-12)". Limited to 500 units worldwide.

configuration.note: "The 3.6 liter six-cylinder boxer engine features two variable turbine geometry turbochargers"

displacementL.note: "3.6 liter". No page opened stated the cc figure; every source gives 3.6 litres, which is the rounded value whatever the exact cc.

drivetrain.note: "provides power to the rear wheels exclusively"

powerHp.note: US rating as published by Porsche (Atlanta release, reproduced by Conceptcarz with "Source - Porsche"). Quote: "The power: 620 hp. The weight: 3,020 lb (1,370 kilograms) in road trim with all fluids on board." The same release is on The Auto Channel (autochannel-2011-911-gt2-rs). Porsche's classic page gives "456 kW (620 PS)" (porsche-classic-997-gt2); Porsche's US arm published 620 hp, used as published. KBB also "620 @ 6500 RPM".

weightLb.note: Standard car (the only configuration: coupe, 6-speed manual). Quote: "The weight: 3,020 lb (1,370 kilograms) in road trim with all fluids on board." Porsche's classic page: "Unladen weight further reduced to 1,370 kg" (porsche-classic-997-gt2).

sources.title: 2011 Porsche 911 GT2 RS Pricing, Research, & Pictures

discrepancies.reason: KBB's 2011 table lists "3075 pounds" for the GT2 RS Coupe 2D; Porsche's release gives 3,020 lb (1,370 kg) in road trim with all fluids. Database entry versus manufacturer figure.
discrepancies.resolution: 3,020 lb used: Porsche's own figure, matched by Porsche's classic-model page (1,370 kg).
